evidence_quotes.quote: Duque de Caxias, one of the most populous municipalities receiving service by this System, experienced a reduction of residences receiving service via distribution network between 2000 and 2010. In 2000, the total percentage of residences receiving service via distribution network was 69% compared with 63% in 2010.

In a significant portion of the municipalities of Duque de Caxias, Nova Iguaçu, Queimados, Belford Roxo, Paracambi and Japeri, the frequency of water supply is usually limited to two or three times a week.

We argue that water access-related problems are directly related to several aspects: the way that water and sanitation services are managed, deficiencies in planning, technical choices, and the way in which existing systems are operated.

Above all, the style of service management has not managed to install complete and efficient water supply systems in the outlying metropolitan municipalities. System incompletion includes various components of these systems: supply conduits, reserve capacity and distribution network infrastructure.

Other sources include: scientific articles; semi structured interviews with CEDAE technicians and managers performed by researchers from the PROURB-FAU-UFRJ Laboratory of Urban Water Research as a part of the Desafio project

criterion_notes.c1: Examines residential drinking-water distribution network coverage and supply continuity across municipalities of the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area (Eastern Imunana/Laranjal and Western Guandu/Lajes/Acari macro-systems).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2 ('include') because it examines institutional and governance factors shaping metropolitan water supply—specifically CEDAE's centralized management model, public sanitation investment policy, priority allocation to industrial complexes and core municipalities, and interstate Paraíba do Sul reservoir operating rules. However, it FAILS the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading ('exclude', E03): its explanatory exposure consists of macro-level infrastructure planning, technical choices, incomplete physical systems (missing treatment capacity, conduits, and storage reservoirs; 40% physical losses), low effectiveness of capital investment programs, and bulk-water hydrology/reservoir management, rather than an empirical analysis of a rule-type legal or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, tenure/documentation requirements, administrative burden, tariffs/cost recovery, enforcement, or analysed ownership/regulatory rules governing household access; CEDAE's 3-day cistern requirement for Minha Casa Minha Vida DPAs and Niterói's private concessionaire are mentioned only in passing without empirical mechanism analysis).
criterion_notes.c3: Multi-source empirical case study drawing on 2000 and 2010 IBGE census data on municipal residential network connections, municipal sanitation plan diagnostic reports, the 2014 State Water Resources Plan, and semi-structured interviews conducted in 2014-2015 with CEDAE technicians and managers under the EU FP7 DESAFIO project.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal residential connection counts and rates to the water distribution network (2000 vs. 2010) and qualitative/operational evidence on supply intermittency (water delivered only two to four days per week via manual switchovers) and unserved peripheral districts.
criterion_notes.c5: Identifies population and unit of analysis (municipalities and residences in the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area), macro-infrastructural/management exposure, connection and continuity outcomes, and an empirical qualitative/mixed-methods case study design.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is published in English (with abstracts in Portuguese, English, and Spanish).

study_design: Multi-source empirical case study (combining secondary municipal census data, official planning/diagnostic documents, and semi-structured interviews with utility technicians and managers)
population_and_sample: Municipalities (18 metropolitan municipalities, focusing on Eastern Imunana/Laranjal and Western Guandu/Lajes/Acari systems) and residential dwellings in the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area, Brazil, plus interviewed CEDAE technicians and managers
exposure: Macro-level utility infrastructure planning, technical system design and operation, low effectiveness of public capital investments (incomplete conduits, treatment, and storage reservoirs), industrial bulk-water prioritization, and river-basin reservoir operating rules
outcome: Municipal rate and count of residences connected to the water distribution network (2000 and 2010 censuses) and continuity/intermittency of water supply (days per week of service)
rationale: Excluded under E03 (Wrong exposure) per the 2026-10-13 Criterion 2 clarification. While the study empirically documents municipal drinking-water network connection deficits and severe supply intermittency in peripheral municipalities of the Rio de Janeiro Metropolitan Area using IBGE census data, municipal sanitation diagnostics, and interviews with utility staff, its explanatory focus is macro-level infrastructure planning, incomplete physical supply networks (insufficient treatment capacity, conduits, and distribution reservoirs), capital investment ineffectiveness by CEDAE, and bulk-water river-basin drought/reservoir management rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access. Under the plain broad wording of Criterion 2, it would be included.
